rules.statement: Do not add host-specific tables such as the Data Protection `DataProtectionKeys` set to a DbContext that ships in a published library; put them in a separate host-owned DbContext.
rules.why: A shared library context that carries host concerns forces those tables on every consumer of the library; a host-owned context keeps the library clean.
rules.check: Look for `IDataProtectionKeyContext` or `DbSet<DataProtectionKey>` (or other host-only entities) added to a DbContext in a packable library project instead of a host project.

rules.statement: Library DI extension methods must not choose where the ASP.NET Core Data Protection key ring is stored (no `PersistKeysToFileSystem`/`PersistKeysTo*` calls); leave Data Protection persistence to the host.
rules.why: The host owns Data Protection persistence, so it can keep the key ring in the same store as the data it protects and reset both together.
rules.check: Look for `PersistKeysToFileSystem`, `PersistKeysToDbContext` or similar key-ring location calls inside library `Add*` service-registration extensions.

rules.statement: Persist the Data Protection key ring in the same database as the data it protects (for example with `PersistKeysToDbContext`), not as files on the local filesystem such as `App_Data/`.
rules.why: If the key ring and the protected data live in different places, deleting one without the other leaves the stored secrets impossible to decrypt, and a reset takes more than one step.
rules.check: Look for `PersistKeysToFileSystem` or new developer state written under `App_Data/` or other filesystem paths when the protected data lives in a database.

rules.statement: When several EF Core DbContexts share one database, give each context its own migrations-history table.
rules.why: The separate host-owned context has its own migrations history so its migrations do not collide with the main context's migrations in the shared database.
rules.check: Look for a second DbContext pointed at the same connection string with no distinct `MigrationsHistoryTable(...)` setting in its provider options.

rules.statement: Every EF Core DbContext that has migrations must be added to the build's pending-model-changes drift check (`dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes`).
rules.why: The drift gate keeps migrations authoritative, so a context left out of it can pick up model changes that no migration covers.
rules.check: A diff that adds a new DbContext with migrations but does not add a matching `has-pending-model-changes` step to the build or definition-of-done script.

rules.statement: In Aspire-orchestrated apps, apply database schema migrations in a dedicated migration worker resource that the API waits on with `WaitForCompletion`, not at API startup; keep data seeding in the API as idempotent seed handlers.
rules.why: A migration failure then shows up as a failed, isolated dashboard resource that blocks the API, instead of crashing the API process.
rules.check: Look for `Database.Migrate`/`MigrateAsync` calls added to the API startup path, AppHost wiring that does not use `WaitForCompletion` on the migration worker, or seed handlers that are not idempotent.
